blockers.message: stage 2-scope-review: owner repair and recertification required; repair every rejected item, refresh all certifications invalidated by the repair, then retry the gate before transition — Step 1 held; resolve research/physics-non-fluid-129-2026-10-21-r2-step1-blockers.json
Batch 16 owner escalation: Worker report requires owner resolution: Acceptance has unresolved findings

Batch 7 owner escalation: The single repair clarified the boundary-value reduction, but both proofs still apply the compact-set integral result to the closed ball without establishing it is measurable and has finite measure. Final review remains unsatisfied, so this is escalated to the owner.
Batch 28 owner escalation: The Statement now correctly says nonnegative, but the proof retains the same strict-positivity defect. This final review remains unsatisfied and requires owner escalation.

Batch 1 owner escalation: The complete current batch and both pages were reviewed. Both prior local findings are resolved, and their proof-context edits do not change public claims or require consumer checks. A remaining local proof gap was found on this second review, so it must be escalated to the owner; no further engine repair is requested.

Batch 34 owner escalation: The complete batch, approved design, and relevant supplier proofs were reviewed. The Penrose argument is otherwise consistent with its stated mathematical route and distinguishes affine incompleteness from curvature singularity; the literature statement has the same geometric scope (see [Senovilla–Garfinkle, Theorem 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.5226)). Acceptance is blocked by an unresolved supplier-hypothesis mismatch.

Batch 6 owner escalation: Rechecked both pages and all six current items. The earlier findings are resolved: the dispersion statement and scope now match the xz-plane circle, and the example defines J_osc=∂tP_1. The cross-batch susceptibility supplier's harmonic-response calculation supports p_1=(ε−ε∞)e under the stated frequency and damping assumptions; that supplier remains draft. One local inconsistency remains: the Example describes q̄ as work of the current on the electric field, while Verification 2.1 correctly treats positive E·J_osc as energy transferred from the field to the oscillator. The single local repair has been used, so this final review escalates instead of requesting another repair.

Batch 2 owner escalation: Both prior findings are repaired: the sphere proof now justifies the null-boundary integral step, and the flat example uses Stokes in the applicable degree. Final review found further unsupported calculations in the flat example; the two-review limit requires owner escalation.
Batch 5 owner escalation: Worker report requires owner resolution: Repair omitted affected consumers

Batch 11 owner escalation: The integral-prerequisite repair and Zank bibliography correction are verified. The remaining source-locator defect was found on this final review, so it must be escalated to the owner. No public interface changed.

Batch 32 owner escalation: Repaired the local area-measure gap and checked all four direct consumers of the changed definition. Owner reconciliation remains necessary for an outside-batch supplier-status gap and the page-level readiness edge described below.

Batch 50 owner escalation: The batch relies on a published mathematical supplier whose proof gap cannot be resolved within this read-only physics scope. The gap affects the finite spectral and operator-norm arguments.

Batch 24 owner escalation: The two round-0 findings are repaired, and the affected consumers’ mathematical uses check out. The revised definition still has a dimensional contradiction; as this is the final review, I am escalating it rather than requesting another repair.

Batch 18 owner escalation: The prior findings are resolved: the orbit definition now specifies its geometry and pullbacks, the Maxwell proof supplies the rotation facts, and the Birkhoff item clarifies the Killing field, smooth coordinate change, and time orientation. The full batch and all listed consumers were checked. One local proof gap remains in Maxwell reduction step 1.1: pulling back to the section y↦(y,p*) recovers the base coefficient, but does not establish smoothness of the sphere coefficient B. This is the second review, so the remaining issue goes to the owner.

Batch 45 owner escalation: The complete batch and relevant supplier proofs were reviewed. Owner reconciliation is needed because the canonical plan and current A page include a fourth prerequisite page that the approved track and prose scaffold omit. I also recorded repairable local proof and hypothesis clarifications.

Batch 26 owner escalation: The assigned inventory and pages are reviewed, and local repairs and consumer checks are complete. Owner review remains necessary for the read-only imported Choice dependency edge.

Batch 9 owner escalation: The repair resolves the prior componentwise-integral and cube-limit issue. Final review still finds unsupported real-completeness uses in the suppliers; under the two-review limit these unresolved issues go to the owner.

Batch 35 owner escalation: The exterior-properties and horizon-generator repairs resolve their round-0 findings. The vacuum-verification repair remains defective: its displayed u-u Ricci numerator is nonzero for allowed parameters. This is the final review after the single local repair, so escalate to the owner.

Batch 61 owner escalation: The six item claims, their proofs, and actual item suppliers are substantively sound within the approved abstract rooted-tree and Laurent-series scope. The approved page-level prerequisite qftx-renormalization-hopf → qftx-causal-renormalization remains unresolved outside this batch, so owner reconciliation is required before acceptance.

Batch 43 owner escalation: The Fubini/Tonelli prerequisites and integrability argument are now supplied, the finite-dimensional argument for R being onto is explicit, and the Teschl locator and sign convention are corrected. A remaining gap in the boundary classification leaves this second review unsatisfied; the one repair round is spent.

This is the final review round, so the remaining prerequisite gap is escalated to the owner.

Batch 29 owner escalation: The assigned items and pages pass. All three round-0 findings are resolved: the null hypersurface normal is distinguished from the surface normal plane and the local auxiliary null field is constructed smoothly; affine parametrization is explicit and the unused dependency is removed; the focal proof supplies extension, smooth ODE continuation, and the endpoint IVT step. Escalate the unresolved downstream future-orientation prerequisite.

This is the final review, so both issues escalate to the owner.

Batch 40 owner escalation: The repairs and supplier uses check out, but ex-gr-fx12-1 still uses Σ_t for both the oriented cut as a subset and the singular chain representing it. This type ambiguity remains after the single repair, so the final review is escalated to the owner.

Batch 57 owner escalation: The three round-0 findings are resolved. Final review found an unaddressed prerequisite gap in the beam-splitter theorem's coherent-input claim, which its loss-channel consumer also uses. Round 1 is the final review, so owner reconciliation is required.

Batch 54 owner escalation: The round-0 findings are repaired, and the affected consumers and supplier arguments were rechecked. The QWZ sign note matches Asbøth et al., Eqs. (2.40)–(2.41) ([source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.02295#page=38)). The final velocity theorem still leaves the domain and global meaning of its Chern-curvature integral unspecified. This is the second review, so the remaining defect is escalated to the owner.

Batch 65 owner escalation: The prior map-action and ODE-convention findings are repaired, and their consumer paths were rechecked. One local issue remains in the scaling Definition: it calls the formal S-map and its conjugate time-ordered systems, although the supplied definition defines a time-ordered system as a sequence of multilinear maps. The finite-renormalization supplier requires two such systems. Specify the conjugated sequence and make the admissibility assumption on that sequence; the direct consumer is prop-qftx-scale-cocycle-law, Facts F1 and Proof steps 1.1–2.1. Since this is the final review, escalate the unresolved finding to the owner.

Batch 52 owner escalation: The seven round-0 findings are resolved, and the listed affected consumers were checked. Final review finds an unresolved scope defect in the metaplectic theorem: its Statement does not specify the admissible time interval, coefficient-path regularity, or solution class defining the propagators in Mp. Proof step 1.2 defines Mp using piecewise-smooth paths, while steps 4.1–6.1 discuss the broader integrable-coefficient class. Since this set is the domain of the claimed group and covering map, the Statement must identify the class and align it with the proof. This is the required second review, so it is escalated.

Batch 93 owner escalation: The prior L²-to-pointwise findings are resolved, and the revised quotient-torus distance and its checked consumers are consistent. One local definition gap remains: the hard-sphere trajectory has no specified time interval or map domains. Since this is the final review, escalate it to the owner. The cited two-state and hard-sphere conventions are consistent with [Codling et al.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2504494/), [Hillen and Swan](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~thillen/paper/HillenSwan12withStyle.pdf), and [Gallagher, Saint-Raymond, and Texier](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1208.5753); these references do not supply the missing local domain.
